feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence from earlier races: iteration 0 (kp 2.5, ki 0.05) and iteration 1 (kp 3.0, kd 0.1) differed by under 0.001 m in max_error. Iteration 4 (ki 0.3) matched iteration 1 almost exactly (oval 0.0615, s-bend 0.0691, slalom 0.0687), so the integral term does not cancel a steady bias. I therefore kept the iteration 4 controller unchanged, so your wheel_radius change is tested alone. Iterations 2 and 3 show that span, lead and body/track changes also leave max_error unchanged, and the narrower track in iteration 3 lowered s-bend progress from 0.15 to 0.13. Interpret the next race as follows. If progress rises above 0.15 and max_error stays below 0.069, speed is helping. Keep wheel_radius 0.035 m and test mass alone next. If progress rises but max_error goes above 0.069, speed is increasing drift. Return wheel_radius to 0.03 m and reduce mass as in request 2. If progress and max_error both stay at iteration 4 levels, speed is not the limit. Test the track as in request 3.
requested_changes: If progress rises above 0.15 and max_error stays below 0.069 on the s-bend and slalom, keep wheel_radius 0.035 m and reduce mass alone from 0.6 to 0.5 kg. Iterations 0 to 4 show progress stuck at 0.10 to 0.15 with no completions, so the next limit is inertia once speed is up. Mass is the cleaner lever, since body_length and track changes in iteration 3 lowered progress.

If progress rises but max_error goes above 0.069, speed is increasing drift. Return wheel_radius to 0.03 m and set mass to 0.5 kg. Iteration 4 shows max_error sits at 0.0615 to 0.0691 across all tracks, so any rise above 0.069 points to speed, not sensor coverage.

If progress and max_error are both unchanged from iteration 4 (oval 0.11, s-bend 0.15, slalom 0.105; max_error 0.061 to 0.069), speed is not the limit. Try wheel_track 0.14 m with wheel_radius 0.035 m and mass 0.6 kg. Iteration 3 showed that narrowing the track to 0.10 m lowered s-bend progress from 0.15 to 0.13, so widening it is the opposite test, and it reduces turn rate per unit of PWM difference.
